analysis.title: US Autos & Industrial Tech: 5 days in 5 minutes
key_insights: US legislators are reported (Bloomberg) to be nearing a deal to ban vehicles from Chinese OEMs. Lawmakers hope to agree as early as this week and aim to send a bill to the President by year-end. Details are still being worked out.

GM targets a 20% increase in robots and automation at its North American factories by 2028 (Reuters), including its own robots built at Kokomo, Indiana and autonomous mobile robots moving parts. GS notes GM is targeting yoy EBIT growth in 2027 and cited automation as a potential driver.

Ford began producing LFP battery cells at BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, with the first cells shipping to Louisville Assembly for Fathom pickup prototypes. Fathom is the first vehicle on Ford's Universal EV platform, with a starting price of ~$28K and sales preorders planned for early 2027.
Innoviz announced a 1-for-20 reverse share split, effective 11:59 pm ET on December 4th. The stock fell 44.2% on the week, the worst in GS coverage.

Keysight reported 4QFY26 revenue, adjusted EBIT margin and non-GAAP EPS above the Street, with record orders of $2,339 mn (up 12% qoq and up 49% yoy organically). It guided 1QFY27 revenue and EPS well above consensus and FY27 revenue growth of about 20%.

GS sees Keysight growth driven by networking/datacenter for AI and A&D, cyclical recovery in wireless and industrial/auto, and deal synergies. Longer-term drivers named are 6G R&D (6G slated for 2029), A&D projects and optical interconnect programs.

Tesla announced Powercore, a solid state transformer that integrates the inverter and breaker in one unit and supports 800V DC datacenter architectures. First units are expected in 2027, manufactured in the US.
Tesla plans to invest $3.1 bn in a Texas polysilicon refinery for solar cells. Construction starts in 2027, initial production in 2030 and full production in 2032.

Texas began re-issuing datacenter air permits under outgoing Governor Abbott (Reuters). About a quarter of new datacenter capacity is slated for Texas, and Governor-Elect Hinojosa has proposed a moratorium.

Tesla began offering select customers the Cybercab for personal use at a starting price of ~$30K, with deliveries expected next month. It requires a $299/month subscription, is limited to geofenced areas of the 5 Texas robotaxi cities, is not for commercial use, and excludes insurance. Tesla's CEO said the fee should eventually fall to ~$115/month and that nationwide availability follows regulatory approval.

Tesla plans to invest over $3 bn in its German gigafactory to build up to 1 mn Cybercabs a year. A building permit application is due before year-end, with construction scheduled for 1H29 and production starting in 2029.
Other Tesla updates: Cybercab rides started in Dallas, the Miami robotaxi geofence was expanded, and FSD (branded Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe) was approved in Italy.
Waymo paused all US freeway operations after California banned its freeway operation and testing last week following safety incidents.

Zoox rides are available on the Uber app in Las Vegas, with an Uber/Zoox expansion to Los Angeles planned for 2027. Mercedes launched an early access program for MB.Drive point-to-point assisted driving in the US and Germany from December 2026. Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries expanded their partnership, with Atlas humanoid testing at GlobalFoundries from 2027.
Pony AI said its Gen-7 robotaxi per-vehicle insurance premium is ~40% of a human-driven taxi's, versus ~50% in 2025.

NHTSA AV data through mid-October shows Waymo with 116 accidents in September and 17 in the first half of October. Tesla self-reported 6 accidents in September and 8 in the first half of October. GS estimates ~215K miles between accidents for Waymo and ~175K for Tesla in September, and ~180K versus ~90K from July 2025 to September 2026. Reported accidents ignore fault and severity, and many are minor.

SuperCompute takeaways for datacenter names such as APH and VRT: companies said demand is strong and customers want to pull projects forward. They flagged slower permitting after the midterm elections and tougher neocloud financing as risks. Pre-fabrication is gaining momentum, services matter especially for liquid cooling, and 800V DC products are expected to ramp at a measured pace in 2027.

Industry data: China retail auto sales are down 25% yoy for November 1-15 and down 22% YTD. October US housing starts rose 3% yoy to 1,309K, above consensus. University of Michigan consumer sentiment was 51.5 in November, the first yoy increase in 23 months.
US Average Marketed Price was ~$52,300 as of November 20th, up ~$2,300 yoy. Active new vehicle inventory was ~3.09 mn units, down ~10K yoy.

market_movers.rationale: 4QFY26 results and 1QFY27 guidance beat the Street, with record orders and FY27 revenue guided to ~$8.6 bn versus ~$8.2 bn consensus.
Announced Powercore solid state transformer, a $3.1 bn polysilicon refinery, Cybercab personal sales at ~$30K and a >$3 bn German Cybercab plant.
Announced a 1-for-20 reverse split effective December 4th, and the stock fell 44.2% on the week.

earnings_insights: Keysight 4QFY26 (reported): revenue, adjusted EBIT margin and non-GAAP EPS were above the Street per FactSet. Orders were a record $2,339 mn.
Keysight guidance: 1QFY27 revenue and non-GAAP EPS guided well above consensus. FY27 revenue growth of about 20% implies ~$8.6 bn versus Street at ~$8.2 bn (consensus estimate).
Pony AI 3Q26 (reported): per-vehicle insurance premium for the Gen-7 robotaxi fleet is ~40% of human-driven taxis, versus ~50% in 2025.
Upcoming: SYM reports 4QFY26 EPS after the close on November 23rd, and CRNC reports 4QFY26 EPS after the close on December 1st.

risk_factors: Midterm elections could slow permitting and delay datacenter projects in some states.
Neoclouds may have a harder time with financing going forward.
A Texas datacenter moratorium proposed by Governor-Elect Hinojosa, with about a quarter of new datacenter capacity slated for Texas.
Waymo freeway pause after California's ban, and AV usability/ODD limits (highways, night driving, geography) that constrain the pace of the AV ramp.
Weak China auto demand, with retail sales down 22% YTD.
geopolitical: US legislators are nearing a deal to ban vehicles from Chinese auto OEMs, with a bill targeted for the President by year-end (Bloomberg).
Datacenter permitting politics: Texas Governor-Elect Hinojosa has proposed a moratorium, and companies flagged midterm election risk to permitting.

tension_points.bull_case: Companies at SC26 said demand is strong and customers want to pull projects forward. Pre-fabrication, liquid cooling services and 800V DC products add growth drivers from 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Midterm elections could slow permitting and delay projects in some states, neoclouds may struggle to finance, and Texas, with about a quarter of new capacity, has a proposed moratorium.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Texas datacenter moratorium under Governor-Elect Hinojosa, or slower permitting after the midterm elections.

theme_stances.key_argument: SuperCompute attendees reported strong demand and customers looking to pull in projects, with 800V DC ramping in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: demand is strong, and if anything customers are looking to pull-in projects

theme_stances.key_argument: Keysight is positioned for strong growth from AI networking/datacenter and A&D exposure, cyclical improvement and deal synergies.
theme_stances.evidence: We continue to believe that Keysight is well positioned for strong growth
